newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EVA Air may move two freighter services to Brussels.
newsitem.headline: EVA Air may move two freighter services to Brussels.

text.p: EVA Air is considering transfering part of its freighter service to Brussels airport from Schiphol, EVA European general manager, Hans Lin told Reuters.
Ideally, EVA would like to have a twice-weekly freighter service into Brussels, while still having a weekly freighter into Schiphol, he said in an interview.
Currently, the carrier operates a three-times-a-week freighter service into the Dutch airport with a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter.
However, the Taiwanese carrier would prefer to operate a passenger service into Amsterdam, also on three-times-a-week basis, possibly using a Boeing 747 Combi.
"We have the traffic rights into Brussels, but we have not decided which aircraft we will operate on the route yet," he said.

Lin said he hoped that the details of the freighter service will be finalised next month. The airline is in the final planning stages of introducing the passenger service into Schiphol and it is applying for slots.
"If the plans go ahead we will have six flights a week into the Benelux. EVA wants to offer a good service to both cargo and passenger market," he added.
"Competition on the Europe-Asia route is very tough and we wanted to make sure that the Brussels route could be profitable before we decided to operate on it."
